title: Board & governance rhythm
summary: The corporate record kept clean: the deck prepped from live numbers, the meeting minuted and signed, the annual budget approved by consent, the state annual report filed.

parts.title: Prepare a board meeting
parts.guidance: Build the agenda around the board's decisions, then attach the financial results, cash forecast, operating updates and draft resolutions needed to make them. Reconcile figures across the papers and resolve missing information with its owner. Agree the agenda with the chair and circulate the meeting package to the board, keeping its version with the meeting record.

parts.title: Keep board minutes on cadence
parts.guidance: Capture attendance, the matters considered and the decisions actually made at the meeting. Follow the corporate-minutes workflow to distinguish discussion from resolutions, confirm the authorized approval process and obtain required signatures. File the approved minutes and referenced materials together; carry unresolved actions forward without presenting them as adopted decisions.

parts.title: Set the annual budget & get board approval
parts.guidance: Turn the operating plan into a budget the board can assess: revenue assumptions, hiring, major spending and cash scenarios. Reconcile it with the latest financial package and explain changes since the previous plan. Use the budget workflow to obtain the applicable corporate approval and preserve the approved version separately from later working forecasts.

parts.title: File state annual report
parts.guidance: Check the entity's actual state registration and reporting obligations against the current corporate record. Follow the annual-report workflow for the applicable jurisdiction and reporting period, with authorized review before filing or payment. Add the filing acknowledgment and any state response to the governance calendar so the next review can identify completed filings and outstanding state requests.
